audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 at 48.24% over 626 games is right: Fizz decides when every trade happens, and Nimble Fighter's flat damage reduction blunts a damage-over-time kit worse than it blunts burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].side was wrong. Rows 0-3, 5 and 6 read 'Skill' where content win[N] and the packet both read Fizz, and row 4 read 'Fizz' where win[4] and the packet read Cassiopeia — the level 6 row was pointed at the wrong champion entirely.
audit.why: Level 6 is your row: Petrifying Gaze is the first tool that punishes the dive. Every other stage is his, because Playful / Trickster falls from 16s to 8s while your Miasma only reaches 16s.
audit.corrected: All seven sides realigned, with the six whys that contradicted their new verdict rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states that Miasma grounds BOTH Urchin Strike and Playful / Trickster, that the untargetable hop eats a committed combo, that Seastone Trident is an auto-attack reset whose wind-up is the tell, or that Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing you.
audit.why: Enemy Q and E are both flagged dash; E is also untargetable; W is flagged autoReset. Your W grounds movement abilities; your R stuns only enemies facing you.
audit.corrected: Ground the commit, bait the hop, and turn into the dive so the R stuns rather than slows.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lint), and dosFull[2].d called Playful / Trickster a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Playful / Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8, Urchin Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Seastone Trident 7/6/5/4/3, Chum the Waters 120/100/80. Fifteen seconds appears nowhere in his kit.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in; the invented figure replaced with 16s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d explained something other than their titles.
audit.why: Each body must answer its own heading.
audit.corrected: Rewritten against Urchin Strike's 550-range dash, the hop, and the R's facing rule.

audit.why: Both packet.suspectNames entries ('Your Petrifying Gaze', 'Save Petrifying Gaze') are false positives; the name matches the kit.

edits.before: Q poke on his last-hits — the poison-into-E pattern starts at level 1 and your DPS already out-trades most mids.
edits.after: Nimble Fighter shaves flat damage off every fang and he walks through minions — your level 1 chip barely registers.

edits.before: W changes the geometry: miasma GROUNDS dashes. Drop it on his engage path and the lane's mobility advantage evaporates.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Urchin Strike and the hop, but on a 24-second cooldown it covers one dive — he simply waits it out.

edits.before: Full kit: Q-poison into spammable E twin fangs is real sustained damage. Trade anyone who steps into Q range.
edits.after: Seastone Trident is 7s at rank 1 and Urchin Strike 8s — he cycles both long before your Miasma comes back.

edits.before: Tear stacking quietly while your E heals off poisoned targets — you win every extended trade from here.
edits.after: Playful / Trickster hits 12s by rank 3 — untargetability returns before your poison has paid for itself.

edits.before: Seraph's/Liandry's spike: your DPS is now the highest in the lane, melee-DPS-carry high. Force extended trades on every cooldown gap.
edits.after: His first item turns the same combo into a one-shot, and your Seraph's/Liandry's DPS needs seconds he never has to give you.

edits.before: Late-game Cass is a hyper-carry: ground their divers, petrify their engage, and machine-gun whoever is closest.
edits.after: Chum the Waters reaches 1300 and picks you before the fight starts — untargetability still beats sustained damage.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your R Petrifying Gaze like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Playful / Trickster: 16s at rank 1 but 8s maxed — the untargetable hop eats your whole combo, so bait it before you spend. - Urchin Strike is 8s and Miasma grounds it. - Chum the Waters is 120s: no open ground while it is up.

edits.before: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Urchin Strike and the hop alike — save it for the moment he commits, never for the wave.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Fizz is executable.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing you — catch him on the way down from Playful / Trickster and the dive dies there.

edits.before: Fizz burns Playful / Trickster on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Playful / Trickster whiffed is 16 seconds at rank 1 — poke freely.

edits.before: That is Fizz’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Miasma is your only answer to the hop — spend it on minions and the dive arrives free.

edits.before: Your miasma is the anti-dive — spending it on poke means the next engage arrives ungrounded and you have no boots to run.
edits.after: Facing away turns Petrifying Gaze into a slow — meet the dive head-on or your one answer to Chum the Waters is wasted.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash on 8 seconds — chase him past your cloud and you hand him a free re-engage.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Fizz wins by going untargetable through your combo, sticking Chum the Waters, and bursting you down before poison ticks.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by outliving one dive: ground the hop, stun the landing, and your fangs beat him for every second he is grounded.

notes: The whole level chart was mis-set on the full layer: six rows said 'Skill' where the content layer and packet said Fizz, and row 4 said 'Fizz' where both said Cassiopeia — the one row you actually win was credited to him. All seven side edits are proposed as one atomic group, and the six whys that would have contradicted their new verdict are rewritten in the same proposal. No paired win[N] edits accompany them because win[0..6] already match the packet exactly. Ratings left alone: they are stage-difficulty numbers rather than side markers, and I could not tell from the kit which way they were meant to read once the sides were corrected. Both packet.suspectNames entries are false positives.
